dining.name: Yorkshire County Fish Shop
dining.priceNote: Fish and chips roughly $13 to $15 as of July 2026
dining.summary: A walk-up window on the United Kingdom waterfront frying fish and chips to order, with lagoon-side tables.
description: Yorkshire County Fish Shop is a small window on the lagoon side of the United Kingdom pavilion selling battered cod and chips in a paper container, plus beer and cider. There are picnic tables along the water directly in front of it.

The fish is fried to order and comes out hot, crisp, and in a genuinely large portion. It is the same idea the dining room next door charges more than twice as much for, and the gap in quality does not come close to the gap in price.
The tables outside face the lagoon, which makes this one of the cheapest legitimate nighttime-show viewing positions in the park if you time it right.
tips: Malt vinegar is on the condiment stand and free. Use it — the chips are made for it and most Americans walk past the bottle.
The waterfront tables here are a legitimate free viewing spot for the nighttime show. Buy dinner at 7 PM, sit down, and stay put.
One order feeds one hungry adult or two moderate eaters. It is a large portion for the price.
The window is on the lagoon side of the pavilion, not on the promenade side where most people look for it.
dining.verdict: Better value than the fish and chips in the dining room next door by a wide margin, and the waterfront tables are the cheapest good nighttime-show seats at EPCOT.

dining.name: Le Cellier Steakhouse
dining.priceNote: Entrees roughly $45 to $75 as of July 2026; expect $80 or more per adult with an appetizer and drink
dining.summary: A windowless stone cellar under the Canada pavilion serving steak, poutine and the cheddar cheese soup people plan trips around.
description: Le Cellier is built below ground under the Canada pavilion as a vaulted stone wine cellar with no windows, low lighting, and heavy furniture. It is a signature-tier steakhouse, which means higher prices and two dining plan credits historically, and it books out further ahead than almost anything else at EPCOT.

The Canadian cheddar cheese soup is the reason. It is a thick soup made with aged cheddar, bacon and a splash of beer, served with a pretzel bread roll, and it has been on the menu essentially forever. People order it who do not otherwise eat soup. It is available as a starter and is the item most regulars would keep if they could only keep one.

The steaks are good and priced accordingly. The filet is the standard order. The poutine is a legitimate side rather than a novelty. Whether the whole meal justifies the check depends entirely on how you feel about paying signature prices in a basement — but the room is genuinely atmospheric and the service is the most polished in the park.
tips: Order the cheddar cheese soup even if you are ordering nothing else you planned to. Everyone who skips it hears about it from the person across the table who did not.
Lunch is meaningfully cheaper than dinner for an overlapping menu, and the room is identical because there are no windows to change with the time of day.
This books out at sixty days for prime times. Same-day cancellations do appear in the app, most often between 2 PM and 4 PM slots.
It is dark and cave-like with no natural light, which some guests find cozy and others find oppressive. Know which you are before spending this much.
The pretzel bread that comes with the soup is the best bread in the park. Ask for more of it; they will bring it.
dining.verdict: The cheddar cheese soup is worth the trip and the steaks are good, but this is signature-tier pricing for a very good steakhouse rather than a great one — book it for the soup and the occasion.

faqs.q: What is Le Cellier famous for?
faqs.a: The Canadian cheddar cheese soup, served with pretzel bread. It has been on the menu for decades and is the single most requested dish at EPCOT.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book Le Cellier?
faqs.a: As early as reservations open, sixty days out, for prime dinner times. Same-day cancellations do surface in the app, most reliably for mid-afternoon slots.

faqs.q: Is Le Cellier worth the price?
faqs.a: It is a very good steakhouse at signature prices in a windowless basement. If the room and the soup appeal to you, yes. If you want the best steak per dollar on property, there are stronger options at the resort hotels.

faqs.q: Are there windows at Le Cellier?
faqs.a: None. The restaurant is underground and styled as a stone wine cellar, lit low throughout. Some guests find it cozy; others find it claustrophobic.

dining.name: Refreshment Port
dining.priceNote: Items roughly $6 to $13 as of July 2026
dining.summary: A small window at the Canada corner of the promenade known for its croissant doughnut and frozen drinks.
description: Refreshment Port sits at the corner where World Showcase meets the walkway back toward the front of the park, beside the Canada pavilion. It is a compact counter selling chicken nuggets, fries, frozen drinks and coffee, plus the croissant doughnut that made it known.

The croissant doughnut is a laminated pastry fried like a doughnut and rolled in sugar, sometimes filled. It is the item people detour for and it is genuinely good — crisp on the outside, layered inside, and warm if you catch a fresh batch.
The rest of the menu is convenience food. What the stand really provides is a last cold drink and a snack at the exact point where most people are heading for the exit.
tips: Ask whether the croissant doughnuts are fresh. They are made in batches, and a warm one and a cold one are different products.
It is the last food stop before the walkway back to the front of the park, which makes it the natural spot to grab something for the walk out.
The frozen drinks here are among the cheapest cold items in World Showcase and there is rarely a line at the drinks side of the window.
Mobile order works and the pickup point is the same window, which regularly saves ten minutes at midday.
dining.verdict: The croissant doughnut is worth the stop if it is fresh and skippable if it is not — everything else here is filler at the corner where you need something anyway.
